questions.stem: Gross Domestic Product is the total value of

options.text: all final goods and services produced within a country in a given period
all goods produced by a country's citizens, wherever they live
intermediate goods used up in production
government tax revenue plus foreign loans

questions.explanation: GDP is a territorial concept: it counts final output produced inside the country's borders, by citizens and foreigners alike. Output produced by Nigerians abroad belongs in GNP through net income from abroad, not in GDP.

distractorRationale.b: Output of citizens wherever they live is closer to GNP, not GDP
distractorRationale.c: Intermediate goods must be excluded or GDP would double-count
distractorRationale.d: Tax revenue and loans are public-finance flows, not a measure of production

questions.stem: NNP is obtained from GNP by

options.text: adding depreciation
subtracting depreciation
adding net income from abroad
subtracting exports

questions.explanation: Gross measures include capital consumption; net measures take it out. NNP = GNP − depreciation. Net income from abroad is what turns GDP into GNP, which is a different step.

distractorRationale.a: Adding depreciation would move from a net figure to a gross one, the opposite direction
distractorRationale.c: Adding NFIA converts GDP into GNP, not GNP into NNP
distractorRationale.d: Exports are already inside GDP via the expenditure approach; they are not subtracted to reach NNP

questions.stem: GDP is ₦700 billion and net factor income from abroad is −₦20 billion. What is GNP, in billions of naira?
questions.explanation: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad = 700 + (−20) = 680. The negative NFIA means factor payments to the rest of the world exceeded receipts, so national product is smaller than domestic product.

questions.stem: The expenditure approach to national income is given by

options.text: C + I + G + (X − M)
wages + rent + interest + profit + transfer payments
value of intermediate goods plus raw materials
tax revenue − government spending

questions.explanation: Spending on an economy's output is consumption plus investment plus government purchases plus net exports. Transfer payments are excluded from the income approach, and intermediate goods are excluded from the output approach, so neither belongs here.

distractorRationale.b: This is the income approach with an error: transfer payments must not be added
distractorRationale.c: Adding intermediate goods causes double counting in the output approach
distractorRationale.d: Tax minus spending is a budget balance, a public-finance concept

questions.stem: A major problem of measuring national income in Nigeria is

options.text: the large informal and subsistence sector that goes unrecorded
the absence of any market in the country
the fact that GDP and GNP are always identical
the CBN's monopoly of note issue

questions.explanation: Street trading, own-account farming and much household production never pass through measured markets, so official GDP understates actual activity. Nigeria has large markets, GDP and GNP differ by NFIA, and note issue is unrelated to measurement problems.

distractorRationale.b: Nigeria has extensive markets; the problem is the activity that stays outside them
distractorRationale.c: GDP and GNP differ whenever net income from abroad is not zero
distractorRationale.d: Note issue is a monetary-policy fact, not a national-income measurement problem

questions.stem: If GDP is ₦700bn, NFIA is −₦20bn and depreciation is ₦30bn, then NNP is
questions.explanation: GNP = 700 + (−20) = 680. NNP = 680 − 30 = 650. Adding depreciation, ignoring the negative NFIA, or stopping at GNP produces the other options. Always apply the two adjustments in order: first NFIA, then depreciation.

distractorRationale.a: This adds both 20 and 30 to GDP instead of subtracting them
distractorRationale.b: This is GDP with neither NFIA nor depreciation applied
distractorRationale.c: This is GNP; depreciation has not yet been subtracted

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines Gross National Product (GNP)?

options.text: The total value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders.
The total income earned by a country's residents, including income from abroad.
The total value of all goods and services produced in a specific time period.
The total income generated from domestic production only.

questions.explanation: Gross National Product (GNP) measures the total income earned by a country's residents, regardless of where that income is generated. This includes income received from abroad, making it a broader measure compared to Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

distractorRationale.a: This definition describes GDP, not GNP.
distractorRationale.c: This is a general description and does not specify the residency of income earners.
distractorRationale.d: This definition focuses only on domestic production, which is not accurate for GNP.

questions.stem: What is the formula to calculate Per Capita Income?

options.text: Total National Income divided by Total Population.
Total National Income multiplied by Total Population.
Total National Income minus Total Population.
Total National Income plus Total Population.

questions.explanation: Per Capita Income is calculated by dividing the Total National Income by the Total Population. This provides an average income per person, which is useful for comparing economic well-being across different regions or countries.

distractorRationale.b: This option suggests multiplication, which is incorrect for calculating per capita.
distractorRationale.c: Subtracting population from national income does not yield a meaningful economic measure.
distractorRationale.d: Adding population to national income does not make sense in the context of per capita calculations.
